title: Scalar compatibility of the normalized projective-line splitting and trace
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. For a standing base $S$, put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ and $q:P\to S$. Let $L_R=R_P(1)[2]$ and let $s_R:R_S(1)[2]\oplus R_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{*,R}L_R$ be the splitting with components the twisted shifted unit and the scalar-extended Kummer class $h_R$ of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Set $t_R=\operatorname{pr}_2s_R^{-1}$ [def-amb-p1-trace]. Use the canonical balanced isomorphisms $T_T(R_T(1))\simeq B_T(1)$, sending $(z\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)b$, and their shifted and direct-sum versions. Let $\beta_q:T_SRq_{*,A}\to Rq_{*,B}T_P$ be the proper counit-transpose map [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Then, under these identifications,
$$\beta_q(L_A)\,T_S(s_A)=s_B,\qquad t_B\,\beta_q(L_A)=T_S(t_A).$$
These equations are equations of the specified derived morphisms and impose no flatness hypothesis on $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Charts: Kummer classes come from Z/ell^n, and the splitting into two free rank-one summands; retained Steps 5 and 6

proof.text: The base $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is finite type over the spectrum of a field. Also $N=\ell^n$ is invertible since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Apply [lem-sp-finite-tate-balanced-scalar-pullback] with $f=q$: use its specified constant, twist, shift and biproduct identifications, and write $D_R=R_S(1)[2]\oplus R_S$. In these identifications $T_SD_A=D_B$ and $T_P(u_A)\lambda=u_B$.

By [lem-sp-p1-kummer-derived-scalar], the upstairs scalar-extended Chern morphisms of the fixed $\mathcal O_P(1)$ satisfy $T_P(c_A)=c_B$ in these same balanced identifications. By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], the two components of $s_R$ are $\operatorname{adj}_R(u_R)$ and $h_R=\operatorname{adj}_R(c_R)$.

The comparison $\lambda_X:q_B^*T_SX\xrightarrow\sim T_Pq_A^*X$ has right mate the specified $\beta_q$, by the proper counit-transpose normalization in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. For $v:q_A^*X\to E$, [lem-pur-adjunction-mate-transpose] gives
$$\beta_q(E)T_S(\operatorname{adj}_A(v))=\operatorname{adj}_B(T_P(v)\lambda_X).$$
Explicitly the B-transpose of the left side is $T_P(\varepsilon_{A,E})\lambda_{Rq_{*,A}E}q_B^*T_S(\operatorname{adj}_A(v))$; naturality of $\lambda$ and the A-triangle identity give $T_P(v)\lambda_X$. This fixes the orientation and the actual comparison arrow.

Apply Step 3 with $E=L_A$, first $X=A_S(1)[2],v=u_A$ and then $X=A_S,v=c_A$. Steps 1 and 2 identify the two upstairs arrows with $u_B,c_B$; the constant-line comparison identifies $q_B^*T_SA_S$ with $B_P$. Thus $\beta_qT_S(\operatorname{adj}_A(u_A))=\operatorname{adj}_B(u_B)$ and $\beta_qT_S(h_A)=h_B$.

For each summand inclusion $\iota_{j,B}$ of $D_B$, Step 1 gives $T_S(\iota_{j,A})=\iota_{j,B}$ and Step 4 gives $\beta_q(L_A)T_S(s_A)\iota_{j,B}=s_B\iota_{j,B}$. The coproduct universal property proves $\beta_q(L_A)T_S(s_A)=s_B$.

Use the specified definition t_R=\operatorname{pr}_{2,R}s_R^{-1} of [def-amb-p1-trace]. Postcomposing the first equation with t_B gives t_B\beta_q(L_A)T_S(s_A)=\operatorname{pr}_{2,B}. Functoriality and Step 1 also give T_S(t_A)T_S(s_A)=T_S(\operatorname{pr}_{2,A})=\operatorname{pr}_{2,B}. Since s_A is invertible, T_S(s_A) is invertible with inverse T_S(s_A^{-1}); cancel it on the right. This proves t_B\beta_q(L_A)=T_S(t_A). All tensor computations were made on K-flat objects, and the other steps used functoriality, adjunction and coproduct identities. No flatness of B over A is used.
